notes.title: Development Update 7: Mask Collection
notes.content:
Last week, we talked about some Mask Upgrades, mainly Mask Tokens and unlock conditions. But how exactly do you use your Mask Tokens? Introducing the Mask Collection!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44539871/36471ba9491e59e9ce010ae17b1b81276fe1600d.png"]

The mask collection provides a convenient list of every single mask in the game, divided in different categories.



Every mask that can be purchased with Tokens has a price displayed, and you can press a button to purchase it directly from this screen.



Also, every mask that you've yet to unlock holds a small hint on how to unlock it. These hints are not particularly specific, but as you keep unlocking other masks, you'll probably be able to figure out what they are by yourself!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44539871/747d18cb182a14beba19f5f675b23d71e3ee3c86.png"]



There are also multiple kinds of mask, and these types are displayed on each mask you've unlocked.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44539871/c1e94e45a13e90f35bec25c935db68c7b5008f15.png"]



Common: They spawn randomly as you play, simply touch one to collect it! They can also be stolen from other players by stunning them.

Rare: They're tied to specific tasks, such as playing a mode as a certain character, or completing a side-challenge in a Minigame. Complete the task and you unlock the mask! You can also steal them from players with a stun.

Premium: These masks can be either purchased or stolen from players. 

Super Exclusive: These masks can only be purchased with tokens. They have no other type of conditions, and also can't be stolen.

Unique: These are tied to the toughest challenges in the game, and they can't be taken from other players. Wear them as as proof of your skill and dedication!



And that's about it! We've given masks a lot of thought during the development of this final update, and we hope that shows. They ended up becoming a quite substantial reward system, and we think they'll provide a lot of extra replayability to Crackpots!

notes.title: Development Update 6: Masks Updates
notes.content:
You may already be familiar with our Mask collection system. it was always a bit of an experiment, but we're finally making some big upgrades to it!



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44539871/edf837e938c1eb799cea8f764b83cc60c1951af9.png"]

First off, we have a lot of new masks prepared for the 1.0 release, and we're still working on increasing that collection! But that's not what we're here to talk about.



In the current version of the game, there's a chance that a mask you've already collected is gonna spawn in the match. This is, of course, completely useless. 



In the launch version, however, you might want still want to collect them, because every time you collect a duplicate mask you'll be rewarded with a Mask Token!



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44539871/90360122f6d7c3443e2dd0664d41d298e6112e96.png"]



Just what the heck is a Mask Token?



They're a brand new kind of currency that allows you to unlock masks you've yet to find! Every mask that can randomly drop in the map can be purchased with Mask Tokens, which will make it a lot easier to complete your mask collection. Or, to just get that one very specific mask that you really want. Just in case you're worried about the mention of random drops and currencies, there's absolutely no real money involved in this, this is strictly in-game content.



Some masks, however, cannot be unlocked with Mask Tokens. They're tied to clearing specific challenges! Minigames, Arcade Mode playthroughs, or earning certain achievements, there's a bunch of different conditions for unlocking them. These masks also can't be stolen by other players in online mode, so if you see someone with one of these masks, you know they completed the challenge!



Come back next week for some more details about masks, there's quite a bit to cover!

notes.title: Development Update 5: Crackpotpedia
notes.content:
We've realized that most PCs load a bit too fast to actually make use of all the tips we've created. That's why we're introducing the Crackpotpedia!



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44539871/ad0b210b1e4fab923275a210f2aca2d30f8f2d9f.png"]

We put every single one of our loading screen tips in this one spot. You you ever want to learn some more specifics about any of Crackpots' features, you can visit the Crackpotpedia to read about it!



We've separated all tips into convenient categories to make specific tips easier to find, and even added a trivia section with some new fun details about all of our characters. Of course, tips will continue to appear in the loading screen, and you can even make use of the Wait on Load option to give yourself more time to read them. But now you'll be able to read them all in one place if you want to!

notes.title: Development Update 4: Arcade Bonuses
notes.content:
We've already talked about Arcade Mode, but there's one last thing we'd like to cover: The scoring system!



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44539871/5611224169c52bb9c43c3b772a9dae871ccb18ab.png"]

When you finish a match, you'll be given a score based on several factors: Remaining time (accounting for all rounds) Rounds Won, Mana Generated (from strikes and potions), Ultimate Power generated (from strikes, shots and specials) and how much damage was dealt to your potiion (the less damage, the more points!).



But the part that's probably a bit more interesting is the special Bonuses. Each bonus has specific criteria, and if you manage to trigger that criteria on any round, you'll be awarded a bonus at the end of the match. Think of them as mini-achievements!



You can already see a few bonuses in the screenshot above. This is what they mean:

FirSt!!1!: You scored the first bullet of the match.

Frontliner: Spent most of your time in the front of the arena.

Too Slow: Your opponent scored a bullet without you ever striking it.

Stun Magnet: All stuns stunned you.

You'll notice that Too Slow and Stun Magnet have a negative value. These are Negative Bonuses, and obviously, you'll want to avoid them! Generally, as long as you manage to play perfectly, you'll avoid any kind of negative bonus, but specific kinds of major mistakes means you get penalized. The vast majority of bonuses are positive though, so don't worry about it too much!



Here's a few other bonuses you might trigger:

Manamanager: Never collected a potion with full mana.

One Step Ahead: Your bottle was never more damaged than your opponent's.

Stun Blocker: Prevented at least 3 stuns with a special move.

Opportunist: Scored a bullet while the opponent was stunned, frozen or cursed

Specialist: All special moves actually struck a bullet

We currently have over twenty different bonuses, but we might end up adding more by the time Arcade Mode comes out. We hope you have fun discovering them all!

notes.title: Development Update 3: Arcade Mode
notes.content:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44539871/02096e5cde93e045268fc0c87d161d4ce8ce8dc4.png"]

We've mentioned Arcade Mode multiple times through development, but we haven't exactly shared any details on what exactly that is. Let's change that!



If you have some fighting game experience you probably know what to expect! Arcade is a single-player, highly replayable mode where you go through several stages of standard matches. Your performance gets scored in each match and will be saved as a high-score once you complete the playthrough!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44539871/e682f9cca7f624baf9f9706e734afc91e5a1eb4e.png"]

Each icon in the lower section of the screen represents a stage. Character icons are standard Crackpots matches (though you'll get a variety of rulesets!), while the bottles represent a minigame. We've already shared some details on the first one in the previous Dev Update, but there's also a second minigame that we'll be showing off at a later date. You'll play a single round of both minigames in each run, and they're both a chance to give your score a serious boost!



The characters you meet in Arcade Mode are randomized, but you'll always finish every run with a match against the beloved Headmaster of the Abracavial Academy. He'll always be the boss!



Since we already have a dedicated Story Mode, we decided not to include dialogue or special story-endings in Arcade Mode. If all you want is continuous gameplay, this is the mode for you! Still, while we may not have story content, you might still get some fun surprises if you finish a run with each character, we hope you check them out!



One more advantage of Arcade Mode over Story Mode, is that you can play Arcade Mode with a friend in local co op! When selecting a character for the run, a second player can join just like in a standard Crackpots match. You'll go through every stage together, even the minigames!



There's still a few more things to cover in Arcade mode, but we'll leave that for another day. Thank you for your time, and we hope you're looking forward to Arcade Mode!

notes.title: Development Update 2
notes.content:
A couple of weeks ago, we revealed some footage of a new minigame. Why don't we take a closer look?



[img src="https://i.imgur.com/NS1uukb.png"]

This is Brick Breaker (WIP name). There's actually multiple ways to play it. The first way is through Arcade Mode, you'll go through a single round in each playthrough, and play to increase your overall score. The second way is right from the menu!



[img src="https://i.imgur.com/upT1lyT.png"]

When playing from the menu you can play two different modes. You can play a single round with any character. This works exactly the same as in Arcade Mode, but completely self-contained. Your score gets saved as a highscore, separated for each character.



[img src="https://i.imgur.com/detKwMo.png"]

The most important factor in your score is your completion time. The faster you are, the higher your score! But if you fail to break all bricks, you'll only be scored on the amount of bricks you managed to break, which is a massive hit to the final score.



The second mode is the Endless Run! As you might think from the name, you play an unlimited amount of rounds, and keep increasing your score until your potion explodes! Damage to your potion carries over from round to round, so even though damage won't impact your score, you have to make sure to finish each round with the least amount of damage taken as you can, or you'll be eliminated!



Damage is not the only factor as you get further in. The more rounds you have completed, the faster the bullets will get! This is a double-edged sword, as it means that bullets will be harder to hit. However, rounds will pass by much faster once bullets gain enough speed, making it even easier to gain more points once you get further into the run!



There's several different brick layouts. No matter where or how you're playing Brick Breaker, the layout will be randomly selected. They all have the same amount of bricks, but you'll have to slightly adapt your strategy on each round to clear each pattern as fast as possible!



If there's anything you'd like to see added to Brick Breaker, let us know in the comments, or in our Discord server down below!



Brick Breaker is just the tip of the iceberg in terms of new additions. Come back next week to learn more more info on other new minigames, game modes, collectables, and QoL changes!

notes.title: Development Update
notes.content:
Hey Crackpotters! It's been a while since we've been able to share anything, but we've been making some great progress on the development side. We're still not quite ready to commit to a date for the 1.0 launch, as there's a lot of things we still need to prepare, so I'm afraid you'll have to wait a bit longer. 

That said, we don't want to just leave you in the dark and disappear again until the release happens. There's a lot of exciting stuff we're working on for the final release and we can't wait to show it off! We'll be sharing some of the things we've been cooking in the following weeks, starting with some brand-new gameplay footage of a new mini-game you'll run into while playing Arcade Mode.

[previewyoutube=d7I_M4bXFLA;full][/previewyoutube]

You can join us on the official Crackpots Discord, let us know what you think!

notes.title: Crackpots second content update is live!
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44539871/f83051520ed8c48403a12c518f55b38faa48964c.png
The second major update was just released! This update represents a major milestone in Crackpots development, because the Story Mode is now finally complete! That's not all! We've also added the brand new core game mode: Push, and all sorts of other types of features and additions, new options, cosmetics, and QoL changes!

Introducing Push mode
Push is a brand new type of ruleset that can be selected as a Game Mode instead of Crackpots or Score. In Push Mode, the giant bottles are replaced by massive totems, and the red barrier is replaced by a huge pillar. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44539871/3454c52e2acf33c350a3cd9a8453ab6e4c6f663a.png

The general objective is the same: Hit the object behind the opponent while protecting yours. However, rather than filling up that object with magical energy, every time you successfully hit the totem, the center pillar will move! Score hits to push the pillar into the opponent's side, stealing space from their play area! When you fully push the pillar into their totem, your opponent gets flattened and will explode in a flash of magical energy, and you win the round! Of course, your opponent can also push the wall into your own area! This mode is a real tug-of-war where both teams constantly push the pillar until either team gets squished! Push is available in both Versus and Online mode, so please try it out!

Story Mode
This is it. The final chapter in the story of The Amazing Crackpots Club. The members of the club will have to face countless trials! Do they have what it takes to be recognized as champions and carve their names into the club's history? Or will their attempts be thwarted by an unexpected foe? Only one way to know!

But of course, before that, it's time for Breezedemus's story chapter! Join him and Clarence as they finally find some time to catch up over a cup of tea. Some truly exciting stuff.

Masks
As a fun way to celebrate the spookiest season of the year, we're introducing a new cosmetic customization feature: Masks!

As you continue to play the game, you'll find a variety of floating masks spawning on the field. After collecting them, a new option will appear in the Character Selection screen that displays a list of all masks you've collected. Choose any mask for your character to wear during the match! They have no impact on gameplay, but they're a new way to show off your style. Collect them all and choose your favorite!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44539871/3aefefa6a909a1e1b076916cf4ff11630e03fe27.png

If you haven't been able to collect a mask through random pickups, you'll also be able to steal it from another player during online matches! If you stun someone wearing a mask, there's a chance that the mask will go flying towards your side of the arena, letting you collect it just like a normal mask!

If someone steals your mask, you'll lose it for the rest of the match. But don't worry! You'll be able to safely re-equip it from your mask collection like normal.

Note: Masks are a very experimental feature, and we're still debating how to treat them going forward. Currently, all masks can spawn randomly during gameplay with equal odds, but we'd like to expand on this system in the future and find ways to make them more rewarding and fun to collect. We'd love to hear your ideas!

And more!
We've added some additional extra features. You'll be able to find new options in the Advanced Rules menu to customize games even further, and also a few QoL changes. If you prefer to play with no distractions, you'll probably appreciate the new Stage Hazard Toggle, which removes all the unique stage gimmicks from each stage while retaining their platform layout.

Full Changelist

New Features

 Breezedemus Story Chapter is now available!
 The Final Story Chapter is now available!
 New basic Game Mode: Push! Score bullets to push the wall into the opponent's field!
 Added Stage Hazards Toggle on Stage Selection.
 Added new Defeat Animations.
 Cosmetic Masks can now be collected and worn in-game.

Characters
Kiyumi & Kitsuro

 Fixed an issue that allowed Kitsuro to hit bullets multiple times with the same attack

Rules

 New advanced setting: Gravity. Affects character gravity, changing how much they can jump and how fast they fall to the ground.
 New advanced setting: Bullet Booster. Multiplies the speed of bullets every time they're struck.

Lobbies

 The match will no longer be canceled if a Spectator leaves the game
 Fixed an issue where the consecutive wins counter would not reset upon a loss.

Misc.

 Music settings on Stage Selection now don't reset after each match.
 Added an option to continue on loading with a button press. Great if you have a fast PC but want to read those tips. (For local matches only)
 Improved Mothilda and Breezedemus CPU behaviour so they strike their own bullets more consistently.
 If you pick a Random character while using a profile, the character will now show up with that profile's palette.
 Adjusted the color of the frozen status effect.
 New non-intrusive tutorial messages were added to character minigames.

Bugs Fixed

 Fixed an issue where difficulty settings in the Gameover Screen would fail to apply until the next match.
 Fixed an issue that allowed characters to use their Ultimate when time was stopped.
 Fixed a bug where bullets would sometimes get permanently frozen inside a Sadie vortex.
 Fixed a bug that would cause the lobby info screen to scale with stage size, displaying some information outside of the screen.
 Fixed a bug where the match would crash when the Freezer tried to freeze a player with a number larger than 4
 Fixed a bug where the Ultimate Charged VFX would sometimes appear in the wrong spot in 4 player matches
 Fixed possible bullet desyncs caused by the shield spirits in Kiyumi's stage.
 Fixed a bug where the main Crackpots theme would loop incorrectly.
 Fixed an issue where the timing of the pause version of Shaken Stirred and Served was different from the normal version.

notes.title: v0.9.1.0 Patch Notes
notes.content:
Today's update includes some upgrades to our lobby system! We've opened up the ability to create 8 player lobbies! Note that this does not enable 8 player matches, but allows more players to join the same lobby and spectate while they wait for their turn. We've also added a 'Wins' counter, these are tracked for each player, and if a player gets a win-streak, the amount of consecutive wins will also be displayed!

Since more players can now potentially join a lobby, we felt like our chat system needed a bit of polish. Chat will be available more consistently through more screens now, and we've also cleaned up some UI inconsistencies. Additionally, during a match, only one chat message can now be displayed at once, so that spectators can't just cover up half the screen with messages.

We'll be looking at all of these systems very closely at today's Play with the Devs!, but if you find any issues yourself, let us know either through Discord, or on the Steam discussions!

Lobbies

 Lobbies can now accept up to 8 players. Only 4 players can play at once, but the remaining players can still chat and spectate.
 Lobby hosts can now force other players to go into Spectator Mode.
 The Lobby Info screen now tracks the wins acquired by each player
 You can now chat in the victory screen.
 In-game chat messages can now appear during character intros and defeat animations.
 In-game chat messages no longer overlap with Player Indicators.
 There's now a maximum of 1 message displayed at a time while a match is active to save on screenspace.
 Lobby Passwords are now hidden when typing.


Bugs Fixed

 Fixed a bug with Mooscles's Custom Palettes where the colors in his toga would sometimes get flipped. If you've already created a palette for Mooscles, you may need to fix it manually.

notes.title: Crackpots first major content update is live!
notes.content:
Crackpots' first content update is here!
Finally, our first major update is live! A ton of new features and pieces of content have been introduced to the game, including a new Mirror Character, a new stage, and new Story Mode content.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44539871/a3683ff36c2324196690af5c29ee2348af7b85f1.png

Introducing Betel G.{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44539871/592a77ce58b2fc7af841b55bab6f581f56ee8388.png

Mirror Characters are new additions to the roster who are based on a previous character, bringing a new personality into existing animations, and adding a new twist to their mechanics! Betel G. is a mirror of Rigel. While Rigel is a lightweight speedster who can adapt to most situations, Betel is more of a heavyweight who relies on precision to reach new heights if he plays his cards right! Here's a breakdown on his abilities:

Strike: Like Rigel's it can be aimed up or down. If he hits bullets with the very tip of his wand, bullets will gain a speed boost! But if he fails, bullets will lose speed instead, making them easier to hit for the opponent.

Shot: Basic 3-level charge shot. The final charge level spawns an extremely slow-moving star, making it easier for Betel to use his other abilities on it. If you strike as soon as you release the charged shot, the bullet will be in the perfect spot for an instant speed-boost!.

Special: This dash is far slower than Rigel's. However, when connecting with a bullet, rather than deflecting it immediately, it'll follow Betel until the end of his dash, where it'll be struck automatically. It's very useful to reposition bullets to the exact position you want them in!

Ultimate: A huge, powerful star bullet. Any other bullets that touch it will be absorbed, giving the star more power. The star moves very slowly at first, but the more bullets it absorbs, the faster it'll move once it's struck by a speed boost from Betel's Strike! Up to 3 Bullets can be absorbed.

Before playing as Betel, you'll need to unlock him in a bonus Story mini-chapter. We hope you enjoy playing as him!

Glacial Garden
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44539871/e9c5300c3a50137da918e3b6a5fe5c7d9b1868dd.png
Moranna's stage: Glacial Garden is now selectable in multiplayer matches! This stage was already available in the story mode, but during testing, we felt that the hazards were not communicated effectively enough for a multiplayer game. We left it out of stage selection to give ourselves a bit of extra time to rework those visual elements, and the results paid off! Glacial Garden is better than ever before, so we finally made it available to all game modes!

Story Mode
We've added 2 additional Story Mode chapters, featuring Moranna and Kiyumi. We won't go into too many details to avoid spoilers, but they're just as featured as the existing chapters, complete with fun shaenanigans, battles, and minigames. Betel G's mini chapter was also added to chapter selection.

And more!
That's everything we have in terms of content, but that's not all that's included in this update! We're also introducing some bugfixes, new features, and even character adjustments. Rigel, Mothilda, Mooscles and Moranna all received important changes to some of their abilities that will have a direct impact on character balance. As always, we're open to feedback, so please try them out and tell us what you think!

We're also making some small adjustments to online lobbies in preparation for a relatively big upgrade, so stay tuned for that!

Full changelist

New Content

 New playable character: Betel G.
 New Stage Theme: The Cooler Wizardboi.
 Moranna's Story chapter is now available.
 Kiyumi's Story chapter is now available.
 Moranna's stage: Glacial Garden is now selectable on VS matches.


Stages

 Vigorous Venue: Many players had issues moving around this stage, making it hard to focus on the bullets, and more on figuring out the best way to even reach the highest levels of the stage. We've reworked the distribution of the platforms to make navigation smoother for all characters, as well as making sure that the trampoline in the bottom floor actually sends all characters to the same spot.


Characters
Rigel

While Cosmic Flare has a lot of utility due to being an extremely strong bullet that can be cast instantly, it tended to become a bit inconsequential if the stun is just removed as soon as it's shot (which happens more often than not), leaving its effects as an ultimate often feeling underwhelming. We've added one feature that ensures that the bullet is always advantageous to Rigel.

 Whenever Cosmic Flare is deflected by an opponent, it'll now lose a bit of speed. If it's struck by the Rigel who originally cast it, it'll go back to full speed.


Mothilda
We believe that Mothilda is in a solid position, but we're making a single adjustment to make her Ultimate feel a bit more consistent in terms of duration, ensuring that the chrysalis always survives for some time if its hit before its most weakened state.

 When Chrysalis blocks a bullet, its damage-over-time timer gets reset.
 To compensate for this, Chrysalis now takes damage passively slightly faster than before.


Mooscles
Mooscles has a lot of advantages, but we nevertheless feel like he falls behind the rest of the cast in a lot of ways. His ultimate, while strong, didn't give you enough time to truly feel like it makes an impact, so we're making his ultimate last longer, while also helping him spend less time shooting. In exchange, he won't be getting his Ultimate as often, but be aware that it's now become a very powerful tool to end a round with!

 Eat Your Veggies! duration increased from 7 seconds to 9.
 Shots can now be charged faster during the duration of Eat Your Veggies.
 Ultimate generation reduced by 25%
 Ultimate generation is now disabled during Eat Your Veggies.


Moranna
We also felt like Moranna needed a bit of extra love. Getting her Ultimate sooner should help her gain control of the battlefield much more easily, forcing her opponents to adapt. Her strike can now also completely cancel her special, which is a subtle change, but can open up more options in moments where you need to move and strike as quickly as possible.

 Ultimate generation increased by 20%
 Moranna can now use her Strike while dashing with Flash Freeze.


Online Lobbies

 Spectators don't use up a player slot anymore.
 The "Rules" shortcut while on lobbies has been replaced with a "Lobby Info" shortcut. Lobby info displays a full list of players in the lobby and their current status, as well as the current list of rules. You can now also open up this list during a match.


Bugs Fixed

 Fixed a bug that could cause the game to crash unexpectedly when ending a match early under certain circumstances.
 Fixed a bug where the Shot Charge sound effect would sometimes continue to play after a charge is canceled.
 Fixed an issue that prevented player names from being displayed in lobby messages.
 Fixed an issue that displayed the wrong player numbers in the results screen if players were not in the default slot order.
 Fixed an issue that prevented character sprites from loading correctly when choosing a random character

Misc. Changes

 Improved network player synchronization when standing on platforms.
 The Giant Knight defeat animation will now only show up on the final round. (there's a chance it'll appear in a regular round that's roughly equivalent to throwing a 12-sided dice 10 times and getting the same result every time, we hope you understand.)
 Optimizations were made to the text system, eliminating short freezes when certain menus were opened.
 Updated Credits.

notes.title: v0.8.1.0 Patch Notes
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44539871/31dab55b5a3e23c92016b85a69199006fa6cf397.png
Crackpots version 0.8.1.0 is now live! 
This is a relatively substantial update that fixes several issues and even adds a couple of new features. Most importantly, you can now change the difficulty of the story mode, perfect if you're having trouble with a specific battle, or are simply looking for additional challenge! The Normal setting is equivalent to previous versions of the Story Mode, while the other two settings were adapted from it by making the CPU values easier or harder.

An important change was made to gameplay that makes it much easier to go down platforms while using either the Tap or Hybrid settings. Dropping from platforms should feel a lot smoother than ever before, but we'll be paying close attention in case we made it *too* easy. Let us know if you're now dropping from platforms accidentally and we'll make further tweaks to the system!

New Features

 Added a difficulty selector for Story Mode: Easy, Normal and Hard settings are now available!
 Online Lobbies now asks players to confirm the controller they'd like to use. A shortcut has also been added that allows you to reassign the active controller without having to leave the lobby.


General

 Going down platforms is now much easier when using the Tap (default) or Hybrid settings.
 Ultimates can no longer be cast while striking a stun bullet.
 You can now only join lobbies created in the same game version you're playing in.
 Fixed an issue that prevented profile controls from being set properly on Single Player modes.
 Fixed an issue that sometimes caused keyboard controls from incorrectly reverting to the original values.
 Fixed an issue when playing with more than 2 players where the wrong amount of characters would sometimes show up at the victory screen.
 Fixed an issue where an additional character would show up at the victory screen when playing with a spectator.
 Fixed an issue where the "Lobby Type" option wasn't properly defining the lobby type.
 Fixed an issue where typing in the chat would fail to block certain shortcuts from triggering, causing the player to do unintended actions on menus.
 Fixed a bug that sometimes caused a fatal error when accepting a lobby invitation.


Characters

 Breezedemus now won't lose his powerups when using Grace of the Hurricane.
 Mothilda's Fleeting Barrier VFX now covers the entire vertical space of larger stages, matching it's actual hitbox more accurately.
 Fixed a bug that caused Breezedemus to maintain the speed upgrade forever if the Speed Wings ran out during Grace of the Hurricane.
 Fixed a bug where Moranna would fail to freeze certain bullets in online matches, resulting in desyncs.


Stages

 The hit-stop effect of the piñata and the ball in Stargazing Spire and Vigorous Venue is now consistent on every strike.


Story Mode

 Fixed the issue of the camera failing to center on Breezedemus on the final duel in Rigel's Story Mode
 Cleaned up some minor typos in certain dialogues.

notes.content:

Ending a match in a timeout now continues to the next screen much faster.  
Pressing Confirm/Start/Enter during the victory screen now instantly takes you to the results screen.  
Getting a Game Over in Story Mode during a section with multiple matches in a row now continues from the last match.  
  
Bugs Fixed:  
  
Fixed an issue that sometimes caused Xbox controllers from being detected as two separate controllers  
Fixed a bug that prevented players from controlling their character when mapping an action to a mouse button in online mode.  
Fixed a bug that desynched the game whenever Breezedemus used his Ultimate in Online Mode.  
  
Dev Notes:  
We've had multiple players report an issue of certain Xbox controllers functioning as two controllers. We believe we've successfully located the problem, but our solution may not be fully consistent with every single controller out there. If you still experience this issue, please let us know and tell us exactly what controller you're using! You can report bugs & issues in our Discord server, or by creating a thread in the Steam discussions page.

notes.title: Early Access Release!
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44539871/0e1ffb9a6c2b77ec46b08cfb93fc9563cda85f9d.png

Crackpots is finally available!

[previewyoutube=lUm2-SOs6Fs;full][/previewyoutube]

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44539871/369857f421120a38fc45f96b9cc4a0e8591cc343.png

After so long, The Amazing Crackpots Club is finally out on Early Access! 

Despite its Early Access status, Crackpots is a very complete package, featuring highly polished gameplay, 7 fully realized characters, 8 stages, and several game modes. You can even setup online lobbies using Steam's peer-to-peer system, or, if your friends don't own their own copy of Crackpots, you can invite them to play via Remote Play Together.

In the current iteration of the game, we have 4 chapters of the story mode. Each chapter is centered around one of our playable characters, and yes, that means that more chapters for the rest of the roster are in the works!

We're cooking a lot more things besides the remaining story chapters. Take a look at the Roadmap for all of our planned Content Updates!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44539871/b5529da01c08d63fb3abb619bcdf1676f0f7835e.png

Our first content update is planned to include story chapters for both Kiyumi and Moranna, as well as Moranna's VS stage. An early version of the stage currently appears on the story mode, but we felt that it needed some additional polish before it's ready to be included on multiplayer matches. Last but not least, we're working on a different kind of playable character we've decided to call a Mirror Character.

Mirror Characters are extra playable characters based on an already-existing member of the club. They share all assets and animations, but the way their abilities work has been remixed to provide a completely unique kind of playstyle. We don't know how many we'll create by the time the full release of the game comes, but the first one is almost ready!

If that doesn't sound exciting enough, a completely unique 8th Character is already in the works! Unlike the Mirror Character, this character was build from the ground-up with its own moveset, design and look. We plan to release it along with the game's 1.0 release, complete with their own Story chapter, and we absolutely can't wait to show it off!

As you can see, there's a few additional game modes on the roadmap, and we'll be sharing some more info on how they work when the time comes. In the meantime, we hope you enjoy the current version of The Amazing Crackpots Club! Don't forget to join our Discord server if there's anything you'd like to tell us. We're very open to feedback, and we'd love to hear your thoughts and ideas, whether it's about content, features, balance, or modes. We hope to see you there!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44539871/b177150c78ade34a9584da2c4f4e7de19e0ce383.png

A new Developer Broadcast is starting soon! 

Join Oscar (Game Director & Programmer) and Ariel (Writer & Music Composer) as they share a small look at some of the content available in The Amazing Crackpots Club's Early Access release!

Click here to watch the broadcast!

We'll be showing-off all playable characters and their abilities, some of the things you can do with custom rulesets, and a look at the first Story Mode chapter (now available in the demo!)
